subject: zoology_2
question_text: Explain how hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism can affect the body.

verification.note: Sourced from 'My Baby Bullet-Q — Senior Inter Zoology' (Star-Q Pass Track Series, Sri Publishers, 2022), book p.34, SAQ 23. The printed exam years are the book's claim, reproduced here as appearances. Zoology-II holds only ONE source book in the corpus, so the two-book union check is structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is our reading of the question and is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

steps.label: Hypothyroidism
steps.why: Iodine is part of the thyroid hormone itself, so too little iodine means too little hormone however hard the gland works.
common_mistakes: Writing that the gland shrinks. In simple goitre it enlarges.
Leaving out iodine as the cause.
steps.memory_tip: Hypo means low: less T3 and T4, and the gland swells trying to make more.
steps.margin_note: Name the hormones and the cause first.

steps.label: Effects of hypothyroidism
steps.why: The same shortage does different damage at different ages, because in a child the hormone is also needed for growth and brain development.
common_mistakes: Using one name for both ages. Thyroid dwarfism is in children, myxoedema in adults.
steps.memory_tip: In the child, growth stops; in the adult, everything slows.
steps.margin_note: Two conditions, one for each age.

steps.label: Hyperthyroidism
steps.why: An overactive gland pours out hormone whether the body needs it or not, so every process the hormone drives runs too fast.
common_mistakes: Writing that T3 and T4 fall. In hyperthyroidism they rise.
Confusing simple goitre with exophthalmic goitre.
steps.memory_tip: Hyper means high: too much T3 and T4.
steps.margin_note: Mirror the structure of the first half.
lines: It is a condition in which the production
of T3 and T4 increases abnormally.
Over-activity of the thyroid may also be
due to cancer of the gland.

steps.label: Effects of hyperthyroidism
steps.why: Thyroid hormone sets the speed of the body's chemistry, so an excess shows up as a raised metabolic rate.
common_mistakes: Giving a lowered metabolic rate. It rises.
Leaving out the protruding eyeballs, which is the marked sign.
steps.memory_tip: Exophthalmic goitre: the eyeballs bulge out.
steps.margin_note: Name the goitre and the metabolic rate.
